text.p: Europe's mobile phone major Nokia Oy said on Tuesday its first-quarter profit raced ahead by over 260 percent, and that this boosted its confidence for further growth and profitability.

Reporting pre-tax profit up at 1.45 billion markka ($278.7 million) from 399 million in the weak year-ago period, Nokia said its net sales climbed sharply to 11.33 billion from 7.93 billion. Earnings per share were up to 3.79 markka from 1.14. ($ = 5.203 Finnish Markka)
The median analysts' forecast had been for a 1.26 billion markka profit and Nokia's stock boosted gains, standing up 10 markka or about three percent to 311.00 markka soon after the report.

"Our first quarter results give us further confidence in our previously stated positive outlook for strong growth and good profitability for 1997," CEO Jorma Ollila said in a statement with the results.
"But as always, actual performance will depend on a variety of external factors, including economic development in our major market areas and industry conditions," he added.
Ollila said Nokia was "continuing to build on our position as the world's number one digital mobile phone supplier and as one of the two leading GSM/DCS network suppliers."
Net sales of mobile phones rose nearly 60 percent to 6.15 billion markka, with telecommunications infrastructure sales advancing over 34 percent to 3.73 billion.

"The operating efficiencies achieved by Nokia mobile phones as well as the continued strong results from Nokia telecommunications enhanced our leading position in many of the fastest growing segments in the telecommunications industry," Ollila said.
